title: Olive, Parmesan and Broccoli Rabe Calzone with Ricotta
changes_from_base: Garlicky braised broccoli rabe with black olives, parmesan, ricotta, sliced mozzarella and chilli flakes replaces the spinach filling in one large calzone.
summary: A single baked pastry envelope holding creamy ricotta, punctuated with salty olives, nutty parmesan and tender broccoli rabe.
equipment: large frying pan with a lid

ingredients.item: broccoli rabe (1 bunch), tough stems removed
fine sea salt or table salt
pizza dough, shop-bought or homemade, at room temperature
olive oil, for brushing and the tray

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 260 °C and lightly brush the baking tray with olive oil.

steps.title: Cook greens
steps.text: Heat the large frying pan over medium, add the olive oil and two thirds of the finely chopped garlic and cook for about 20 seconds until aromatic but not yet coloured, add the broccoli rabe and 3 tbsp water, raise the heat to medium-high and cook for 3 min, then lower the heat, cover with a lid and cook for a further 2–3 min until the thick stems are tender, season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: On a lightly floured work surface, stretch or roll out the pizza dough to a 30 cm round.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spoon the ricotta over one half of the round leaving a 1 cm border, sprinkle the finely grated parmesan over the ricotta, add the remaining chopped garlic, top with the sliced fresh mozzarella, pile the cooked broccoli rabe on top and scatter with the thinly sliced black olives and the dried chilli flakes.

steps.title: Seal
steps.text: Wet the outer edges of the dough with water, fold over to cover the filling and press the edges firmly together to seal.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.text: Lift the sealed calzone onto the oiled tray and brush the top with olive oil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 15–20 min until the pastry is golden and firm to the touch, cool for 5 min before serving.

tips: Cook the broccoli rabe gently so the tender leaves stay bright green; if you rush it on high heat, they will wilt and darken unevenly.
Pat the cooked greens dry with a clean tea towel before adding them to the calzone so excess moisture doesn't soften the pastry base.
Scatter the olive slices on top rather than mixing them in so you get a hit of their salty flavour in each bite.
storage: Cool and refrigerate for up to 2 days, reheating gently if desired. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
